claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal boundaries in the coarse lamellar colonies act as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tensile deformation.

The proposed intervention consists of cryogenic rolling at approximately strain 1.2, warm rolling at approximately 600 °C and strain 1.2, and rapid annealing at approximately 850 °C for 30–50 seconds with a heating rate near 15 K/s.
The hybrid processing route will significantly refine the duplex lamellar structure and reduce colony spacing.
The hybrid processing route will enhance interfacial coherence and make internal boundaries tougher and less susceptible to microcrack initiation.
Cryogenic deformation raises dislocation density and stored energy in the alloy.
Subsequent warm rolling and rapid annealing use the deformation-induced stored energy to promote controlled partial recovery and nanocrystallization.
The resulting grain refinement enhances tensile strength.
Improved interface toughness arrests microcrack propagation and thereby enhances room-temperature ductility.
In-situ microstructural monitoring enables the beneficial structural changes to be achieved consistently.
The processed alloy will have greater tensile yield strength than the unmodified coarse-lamellar baseline.
The processed alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified coarse-lamellar baseline.
Conventional processing produces coarse lamellar colonies with brittle internal boundaries that cause premature microcracking and limited tensile ductility despite high strength.
Substantial deviations from the specified rolling and annealing conditions may cause excessive refinement or coarsening and negate the proposed benefits.
Process variability may alter the balance between deformation-induced defects and annealing-induced recovery and thus affect the degree of improvement.
